skill.name: web-search
skill.description: Adds web search, direct answers, and webpage extraction through inference.sh belt apps for Tavily and Exa.
skill.summary: Search the web and extract page content through Tavily and Exa apps.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: The skill is not malicious and no prompt-injection attempt was found in SKILL.md. Confirmed risk comes from intentional use of the external belt CLI for web search, URL extraction, LLM workflows, and a broad Bash(belt *) permission. Many static hits were Markdown formatting or documentation links and were dismissed as false positives.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the exact belt app run commands required for Tavily and Exa, or document why full belt access is required.

remediation.issue: External search and extraction services receive user queries and URLs
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to send secrets, private URLs, or regulated data to Tavily, Exa, inference.sh, or OpenRouter workflows.

remediation.issue: Remote setup and media links depend on external hosts
remediation.suggestion: Pin setup guidance to a reviewed release and consider packaging marketplace images locally instead of loading remote image URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Tool Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows Bash(belt *), which permits any belt subcommand rather than only the documented search and extraction commands. This broad scope increases misuse risk if prompts or workflows request unrelated belt actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools line explicitly grants the belt wildcard, and the rest of the file documents narrower search and extraction use cases. The risk is permission breadth, not malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Research tasks need current web sources and clean page text. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to Tavily and Exa through the inference.sh CLI.
actual_capabilities: Runs Tavily search assistant queries through belt app run tavily/search-assistant.
Extracts text and images from one or more URLs with Tavily Extract.
Runs Exa Search for relevant links with context.
Requests direct factual answers with Exa Answer.
Chains search or extraction outputs into OpenRouter Claude prompts through belt.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and login before use.
Sends search queries and target URLs to external services.
Result quality depends on Tavily, Exa, and indexed web content.
It does not verify facts without source review.

use_cases.title: Source Collection
use_cases.description: Gather current links and summaries for a research question before drafting a report.

use_cases.title: RAG Input Discovery
use_cases.description: Find and extract web pages that can seed a retrieval-augmented generation workflow.

use_cases.title: Claim Checking
use_cases.description: Search for supporting sources and conflicting evidence before publishing a factual claim.

prompt_templates.title: Find Recent Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Search the web for recent, reliable sources about [topic]. Return key findings and source links.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Page Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract readable content from these URLs: [URLs]. Summarize each page separately.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Search Providers
prompt_templates.scenario: Quality review across Tavily and Exa
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Tavily and Exa searches for [topic]. Compare result relevance, source quality, and gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Briefing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced search, extraction, and synthesis workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic], extract the three strongest sources, then prepare a sourced briefing for [audience]. Note limitations.

output_examples.input: Search for recent AI agent evaluation methods.
output_examples.output: A sourced research brief with key methods, source links, publication context, and notes on recency.

output_examples.input: Extract content from a long article URL.
output_examples.output: Clean article text, important images when available, and a concise summary of the page.

output_examples.input: Ask Exa for a direct factual answer about a public statistic.
output_examples.output: A brief answer with supporting source links and a reminder to verify current figures.

best_practices: Use specific queries with dates, geography, and source requirements.
Review cited sources before using results in decisions.
Avoid sending secrets, private URLs, or regulated data to search providers.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated answers as verified facts without source review.
Do not extract pages that forbid automated access.
Do not run broad CLI commands outside the documented search and extraction flows.

faq.question: Does this skill require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a completed belt login.

faq.question: Which search providers does it use?
faq.answer: It documents Tavily Search, Tavily Extract, Exa Search, Exa Answer, and Exa Extract.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it browse the web directly?
faq.answer: No. It invokes inference.sh belt apps that call external search and extraction providers.

faq.question: What data may leave my environment?
faq.answer: Search queries, URLs, extracted content, and LLM prompts may be sent to external services.

faq.question: Can it fact-check information?
faq.answer: It can gather sources for fact-checking, but users must review the sources and evidence.
